title: Acyclic Hom from bounded-above acyclic sums of Ext-orthogonal modules
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site in the chosen universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $F$ an $R$-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $(E_i)_{i\in I}$ be a set-indexed family of $R$-module sheaves such that $\operatorname{Ext}_R^p(E_i,F)=0$ for every $i\in I$ and $p>0$, where $\operatorname{Ext}_R^p(E_i,F)=H^p\operatorname{Hom}_R(E_i,J^\bullet)$ for an injective resolution $F\to J^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let $K^\bullet$ be a bounded above acyclic cochain complex of $R$-module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules], and suppose every $K^n$ is isomorphic to a small coproduct of members of this family, with repetitions allowed. Then the cochain complex of abelian groups $\operatorname{Hom}_R(K^\bullet,F)$ is acyclic. Its term in degree $n$ is $\operatorname{Hom}_R(K^{-n},F)$ and its differential sends $h$ to $(-1)^{n+1}h\circ d_K^{-n-1}$.

source.place: Tag 07AA, example-hom-complex-into-sheaf, second spectral sequence, with the coproduct/Ext-orthogonality application written in the proof of lemma-existence-derived-lower-shriek.

proof.text: Work in $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$. Since the site is small in the module universe, [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] makes $\mathcal A$ Grothendieck abelian. By [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] it has enough injectives, and clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] gives an exact augmented injective resolution $0\to F\xrightarrow{\iota}J^0\to J^1\to\cdots$, extended by zero for negative degrees. Fix this resolution for every Ext calculation. This is legitimate: by [lem-sp-derived-well-defined], applied to the left exact additive functor $\operatorname{Hom}_R(E_i,-):\mathcal A\to\operatorname{Ab}$ (and to $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,-)$ for the coproducts $M$ of step 2), the groups $H^p\operatorname{Hom}_R(E_i,J^\bullet)$ do not depend on the chosen injective resolution of $F$, so the hypothesis $\operatorname{Ext}^p_R(E_i,F)=0$ for $p>0$ holds for this $J^\bullet$.

source.place: Tag 07AA, example-hom-complex-into-sheaf, choice of injective resolution; injectives.tex Tag 079Q, remark-existence-D; derived.tex Tag 013K, lemma-injective-resolutions-exist (1).

proof.text: If $M\simeq\bigoplus_{a\in A}E_{i(a)}$, restriction to summands gives a degreewise isomorphism of complexes $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,J^\bullet)\simeq\prod_{a\in A}\operatorname{Hom}_R(E_{i(a)},J^\bullet)$: postcomposition by $d_J$ commutes with restriction. For complexes $L_a$, apply the exact-product statement [lem-pc-abelian-groups-exact-products] to $0\to Z^q(L_a)\to L_a^q\to B^{q+1}(L_a)\to0$ and $0\to B^q(L_a)\to Z^q(L_a)\to H^q(L_a)\to0$. Kernels are computed componentwise, so these two exact product sequences identify $H^q(\prod_aL_a)$ with $\prod_aH^q(L_a)$. Thus $\operatorname{Ext}_R^q(M,F)=0$ for $q>0$. The argument includes an empty coproduct and arbitrary repetitions.

source.place: Tag 07AC, lemma-existence-derived-lower-shriek, passage from vanishing on free summands to vanishing on their direct sums; the product-cohomology calculation is written out here.

proof.text: Choose an integer $b$ such that $K^r=0$ for $r>b$. Define the first-quadrant double complex $D^{p,q}=\operatorname{Hom}_R(K^{b-p},J^q)$ for $p,q\ge0$, with zero terms elsewhere, horizontal differential $d_I(h)=h\circ d_K^{b-p-1}$ and vertical differential $d_{II}(h)=d_J^q\circ h$. Both differentials square to zero and they commute, since postcomposition and precomposition commute. The boundary at $p=0$ is compatible with extension by zero because $K^{b+1}=0$. This is the commuting convention of [def-sp-double-complex-total], whose total differential is $d_I+(-1)^pd_{II}$. Each total diagonal is finite: $0\le p,q\le p+q$.

source.place: Tag 07AA, example-hom-complex-into-sheaf, the Hom double complex, reindexed using the upper bound; homology.tex Tag 012Z, section-double-complex.

proof.text: The $p$-th column is $\operatorname{Hom}_R(K^{b-p},J^\bullet)$. By step 2 and the coproduct hypothesis its positive cohomology vanishes. In degree zero, the exact augmentation identifies $F$ with $\ker(d_J^0)$, so the kernel universal property identifies $\ker(\operatorname{Hom}_R(K^{b-p},d_J^0))$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_R(K^{b-p},F)$; there are no negative-degree boundaries. These identifications commute with precomposition by $d_K$. Therefore the degree-zero column cohomology, with its horizontal differential, is the complex $C^p=\operatorname{Hom}_R(K^{b-p},F)$, $d_C(h)=h\circ d_K^{b-p-1}$ for $p\ge0$.

source.place: Tag 07AA, example-hom-complex-into-sheaf, column cohomology; Tag 07AC, lemma-existence-derived-lower-shriek, the row $E_1^{p,0}$.

proof.text: Every row $D^{\bullet,q}$ is exact, directly from acyclicity and injectivity [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules, def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Indeed, write $r=b-p$. A horizontal cocycle $h:K^r\to J^q$ kills $\operatorname{im}d_K^{r-1}=\ker d_K^r$, so it factors through $K^r/\ker d_K^r=\operatorname{im}d_K^r$. If $p>0$, extend this factored map across the monomorphism $\operatorname{im}d_K^r\hookrightarrow K^{r+1}$ using injectivity of $J^q$; the extension $g$ satisfies $h=g\circ d_K^r$, so $h$ is a horizontal boundary. If $p=0$, then $r=b$ and $d_K^b=0$, hence the factorization already gives $h=0$. This proves exactness also at the left endpoint, without any assertion about sectionwise exactness of $K$.

source.place: Tag 07AA, example-hom-complex-into-sheaf, the other filtration of the Hom double complex; row exactness is expanded using the definition of injectivity.

proof.text: Apply the second spectral sequence of [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] to $D$. Its first page is ${}''E_1^{q,p}=H_I^p(D^{\bullet,q})=0$ by step 5. All later pages and all stable terms are consequently zero. For each $n\ge0$, the cited theorem gives a finite filtration $H^n(\operatorname{Tot}D)=F^0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq F^{n+1}=0$ whose successive quotients are these stable terms. Descending induction, from $F^{n+1}=0$ and $F^i/F^{i+1}=0$, gives $F^i=0$. Hence $H^n(\operatorname{Tot}D)=0$ in every degree (negative total degrees are already zero).

source.place: Tag 07AA, example-hom-complex-into-sheaf, the two filtrations; convergence is homology.tex Tag 0132, lemma-first-quadrant-ss.

proof.text: For the first spectral sequence of [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences], step 4 gives ${}'E_1^{p,q}=0$ for $q>0$ and ${}'E_1^{p,0}=C^p$, with $d_1=d_C$. Thus ${}'E_2^{p,0}=H^p(C)$ and ${}'E_2^{p,q}=0$ for $q>0$. Its finite-filtration convergence satisfies exactly the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-first-quadrant-row-collapse]. Applying that lemma in every degree $p\ge0$, including $p=0$, gives $H^p(C)\simeq H^p(\operatorname{Tot}D)=0$ by step 6. In particular it is the whole edge-isomorphism assertion, rather than only the positive-degree corollary, that is used.

source.place: Tag 07AC, lemma-existence-derived-lower-shriek, final spectral-sequence paragraph; Tag 07AA, example-hom-complex-into-sheaf; homology.tex Tag 0132, lemma-first-quadrant-ss.

proof.text: Finally put $T^n=\operatorname{Hom}_R(K^{-n},F)$ with the differential in the statement. Degree relabelling gives $T^{p-b}=C^p$ for $p\ge0$ and $T^n=0$ for $n<-b$. On this relabelled complex the differential is $(-1)^{p-b+1}d_C$. Choose signs $a_0=1$ and $a_{p+1}=(-1)^{p-b+1}a_p$. Multiplication by $a_p$ gives an isomorphism from $C^p$ to $T^{p-b}$, since $a_{p+1}d_C=(-1)^{p-b+1}d_Ca_p$; its inverse is multiplication by the same signs. It therefore identifies $H^p(C)$ with $H^{p-b}(T)$. These groups vanish by step 7, and all lower degrees of $T$ are zero. This proves acyclicity with precisely the specified Hom differential.

source.place: Tag 07AC, lemma-existence-derived-lower-shriek, concluding acyclicity of the Hom complex; explicit sign comparison with the convention in the item.
